title: Mistral API Free Tier: Limits, Models & Credits (2026)
summary: Mistral API free tier has no upfront cost but imposes rate limits, token caps, and data restrictions. Decide whether its constraints work for your project.
body_markdown:
## Hidden limits and terms behind the free tier


Before the first request went out, every constraint that caused the failure was already published by Mistral, in the documentation or in the account console.


Nothing was hidden; the habit of not reading a free plan's terms the way you would read a contract did the hiding.


Below are the limits a team would have found on day one, each with the date it was published or changed. They are requests per second, tokens per minute, the monthly token cap, model access by tier, phone verification, data-use terms and limit revisions.


Take from it that no single limit was the trap. The trap was that they bind at different moments, so passing one check tells you nothing about the others.


### Rate limits versus monthly token caps


In the middle of a burst, a per-minute limit throttles you, and your retry logic can absorb that. A monthly token cap doesn't throttle, it stops you, and it does so at whatever point in the cycle your usage crosses it.


Usually that's late in the month, when the pipeline is busiest and the team has stopped watching it.


Phone verification belongs here too: the account is tied to one person's number, so if that person leaves, the whole workflow depends on a credential nobody else controls.


### Data-use terms on the free tier


Free access is often paid for in data rights.


Read the terms for whether your prompts and outputs can be used to improve the provider's models, because that clause decides whether customer text, internal documents or source code can go through the free tier at all.


If your legal team would say no to a paid vendor with those terms, the answer is the same here. Finding out after launch is the expensive way to learn it.


### Model access and limit changes over time


**Free keys don't always reach every model** . The strongest one you benchmarked may sit behind a paid tier, which means your quality testing and your production ceiling can describe different products.


Limits also move. A figure you planned around in one quarter can be revised in the next, and a free tier doesn't have a commitment to keep it.


So the working habit is to date every limit you rely on and recheck it on a schedule, which is what the next section sets up.
